title: Missing Digit Detective
context: Grade 4, and the one place in this chapter where a child has to reason rather than follow a procedure. An adult sees a puzzle. What the page is actually doing is testing whether the carrying of the previous topic was understood or only copied, because a missing digit cannot be found by anybody who does not know where the carried one came from and where it went.

writeup.why: Find the digits somebody has hidden in a finished sum, using nothing but the column each one sits in.
writeup.look: A completed column sum with small cards over some of its digits, and a reasoning strip that opens under whichever column is tapped.
writeup.stage: Three bands across 1600 by 900. The header runs 0 to 80 and is one line only: 'Missing Digit Detective' in ink at the far left, a small dot set clear of the name by measuring it, the phase title beside the dot on the same line, the host's navigation, and again, sound and restart as three round controls at the far right. The canvas runs 92 to 746, one rounded card on the paper colour. At its top left, at 64,108 and 330 by 76, sits the running count: the cards lifted against the cards lying on the sum, two numbers in ink, the first climbing by one as each hidden digit is found; on the fourth phase it carries instead the columns checked forwards against the columns in the sum. Nothing in it ever counts down and nothing in it ever reads as a score. The working area is 1086 by 528 at 64,202. The mat sits across the top of the working area, 800 by 320 at 207,202: a circle band 56 tall along its top with one circle 48 across over every column but the ones, then headings 40 tall, then two addend rows of cells 68 tall, then a rule 6 tall, then the answer row 68 tall beneath it, with the columns 120 wide. A cover card is 96 by 76 and lies on top of an addend digit with a lift tab drawn at its corner, so it reads as something laid down rather than as an empty square; no cover card is ever laid on the answer row, and the answer digits stay in green all the way through. Tapping a column opens the reasoning strip beneath the mat, 1086 by 128 at 64,538: the known digits of that column drawn again in deep blue and set apart from each other, the gap drawn as an amber square, the answer digit in green under a short rule of its own, and any digit standing in the circle above brought down into the strip in vermilion beside the rest. A column tapped before the column to its right is settled is refused: the strip does not open, the column that has to come first is lit with its heading named, and not one digit of the refused column is shown. Settling a column whose total passes nine sends its carry up into the circle above the next column by itself, where it stays in sight for the rest of the sum. The too small light rings an answer digit in amber wherever it is smaller than a digit standing above it, and writes that reading out in words underneath. The forward check band runs 1086 by 56 at 64,674: the completed sum is added again from the ones, one column at a time, its total laid under the answer that was printed with the two rules aligned, each agreeing column ticked in green as it is passed and the first column that parts them, if there is one, lit amber and left lit. The build your own bay takes the reasoning strip's rectangle and holds a blank mat, a pad and a stack of cover cards. Down the right of the canvas, in the same rectangle on every phase and never animated in or out, the question sits above the answer slot at 1186,250 (356 by 92) that holds what the child has given, and under it the pad at 1170,368 (388 by 363). The pad is twelve number keys three across wherever a hidden digit is asked for, and on the third and fourth phases a choice pad of large keys in the same rectangle, reading carried and not carried on the third and agrees and does not agree on the fourth, so that a reading can be given as well as a digit. The footer runs 758 to 900: the voice caption at the far left with its speaking dot beside it, measuring its own wrap and dropping a type size rather than spilling, and the phase bar at the right with the question count under it. There is no sidebar and no score box anywhere, and nothing is ever written over the working area. Content colours are the chapter's own: a number being added is deep blue, the answer standing under the rule is green, a digit carried into the next column is vermilion, a rounded number is rose, the digit under discussion or the one that is missing is amber, and a zero that is only holding a place open is grey. Chrome never borrows one of them, and every one of those readings survives with the colour taken away, because a column is told by the heading written above it before it is ever told by a colour, and a carried digit by being small and by sitting above the column it is going into.
writeup.finish: The card shows the hardest sum the child completed, with the digits they found still lit and the forward check standing beside it.

phases.win: the card lifts and the column reads correctly in both directions
phases.does: works out the only digit that makes the column come out right
phases.goal: a column with one digit missing has only one digit that fits
phases.says: The answer is showing. Work backwards to the digit that is hidden.
phases.check: Away from the screen: a ones column adds two and a hidden digit, the answer digit is eight and nothing is carried. What was hidden?
phases.feels: the answer is showing all along, so the hidden digit has nowhere to hide
phases.hands: Write a correct column sum on paper, cover one digit of the top number with a small square of card, and hand it to somebody else to find. Then swap over and do it again with a different column covered.
phases.tries: A miss is answered three ways at once and none of them is the answer. First rung, from the item's own miss line: what is showing in this column? Second rung, the phase's: what does the column have to come to? Third rung: the column is left on the mat on its own with its known digit drawn in tokens and the answer drawn in tokens beside it. The number pad stays open behind all three.

wrong.why: the answer digit is the only number showing in that column, and a square that wants a number takes the number nearest to hand.
wrong.move: writes the answer digit into the covered square.
wrong.screen: the reasoning strip opens under the column with its three squares drawn well apart, the two above the rule and the answer under it, the known digit in deep blue and the gap in amber; the column is then read out as one sentence, this and the gap make the answer, with the child's digit still standing where it was put.

wrong.why: a column has only ten digits that could go in it, and trying them is quicker than thinking about them.
wrong.move: tries digits one after another until one of them is accepted.
wrong.screen: the strip stands the tokens of the known digit in the column beside the tokens the answer calls for, both stacks countable at a glance, so the space between the two stacks is the digit that is missing. Nothing is cleared and no digit is refused.

phases.screen: a ones column showing one digit, a covered card and the answer digit
phases.soWhat: With the answer and all but one digit of a column known, the missing digit is fixed.
phases.concept: A column can be read backwards

phases.win: the ones column settles and a carry appears above the column to its left
phases.does: taps a middle column, is told which column comes first, and starts at the ones
phases.goal: the ones column is the only one nothing can carry into
phases.says: Start at the ones. Nothing can carry into it.
phases.check: Why can a missing digit in the hundreds column not be found before the tens column has been settled?
phases.feels: one column can be read straight away and every other one has to wait its turn
phases.hands: Take a sum with three digits covered and ask which one can be found first. Do not let anything be written down until that question has been answered out loud and the reason given.
phases.tries: First rung, from the item: which column is furthest to the right? Second rung, the phase's: what could be arriving in this column that you do not know about yet? Third rung: every column but the ones is covered over and only that one is left to be read. The number pad stays open.

wrong.why: the left is where reading begins, and one gap looks as good a place to begin as another.
wrong.move: taps the leftmost covered column first, because its gap looks the easiest to fill.
wrong.screen: the column is refused, the strip does not open, and the column that has to be settled first is lit with its heading named; the covered digit stays covered and nothing whatever about the refused column is given away.

wrong.why: the column is finished, so it looks as though there is nothing left in it to take along.
wrong.move: settles the ones column and moves left without taking anything with it.
wrong.screen: the tokens of the settled ones column are counted out and ten of them tie and walk left into the circle above the tens, where the carried digit stays in vermilion while the tens column is read again with it standing in place; the digit the child gave stays in the answer slot beside the reading.

phases.screen: a sum with cards in three columns and every column tappable
phases.soWhat: Nothing can carry into the ones column, so it is the only column that can be read on its own.
phases.concept: Start at the ones here too

phases.win: the too small light comes on and the carry is drawn into the next circle
phases.does: works out what the column really came to and where the rest went
phases.goal: an answer digit smaller than the digits above it means a carry left
phases.says: The answer digit looks too small. Where did the rest of it go?
phases.check: A column adds eight and seven and the answer digit is five. What happened in that column, and what went left?
phases.feels: the answer digit is smaller than the numbers that made it, and that is the clue rather than the trouble
phases.hands: Write a column where seven and five are added and the answer digit is two, and ask whether that can possibly be right. Let the argument run for a while before you settle it.
phases.tries: First rung, from the item: is the answer digit bigger or smaller than the digits above it? Second rung, the phase's: what does a column keep when it passes nine? Third rung: the column is filled with tokens and the child ties ten of them and reads what is left. The choice pad stays open.

wrong.why: adding has always made things bigger, so an answer smaller than what went into it looks like a mistake on the page.
wrong.move: says the sum has been printed wrong, because the answer digit is smaller than both digits above it.
wrong.screen: the column is filled with its tokens and counted: they pass nine, ten of them tie and walk left into the circle above the next column, and what is left standing in the column is exactly the answer digit that was printed. The child's verdict stays in the answer slot beside it.

wrong.why: the column in front of you can be made to work on its own, and the small digit sitting above it is easy to look past.
wrong.move: finds a digit that makes the column come out without allowing for the carry coming into it.
wrong.screen: the circle above the column is lit and its digit is drawn down into the reasoning strip with the rest, and the column is counted again with everything that is standing in it; the two readings stand one under the other and what lies between them is the carried digit itself.

phases.screen: a tens column whose answer digit is smaller than both digits above it
phases.soWhat: An answer digit smaller than a digit above it means the column passed nine and a carry left it.
phases.concept: A carry explains an answer that looks too small

phases.win: the two answers stand together and agree, column by column
phases.does: adds the whole sum forwards against the answer that was printed
phases.goal: a finished hunt is only finished once it has been added forwards
phases.says: Now add the whole thing forwards. Does it come to the answer that was printed?
phases.check: You have filled every gap in a sum. What do you do before you say that it is finished?
phases.feels: the hunt is over and the sum still has to be added the ordinary way
phases.hands: Once every covered digit has been found, write the completed sum out fresh on clean paper and add it the ordinary way. Hold it against the answer that was printed before anybody is allowed to say they have finished.
phases.tries: First rung, from the item: which column does the forward check begin at? Second rung, the phase's: what must the total it builds come to? Third rung: the sum is cut to two columns and the child adds those two forwards against the printed answer. The choice pad stays open.

wrong.why: every column was reasoned out one at a time, so working the same columns again looks like doing the whole job twice.
wrong.move: lifts the last card and calls the hunt finished without adding anything forwards.
wrong.screen: the mat works the completed sum forwards from the ones, one column at a time, and lays its total under the answer that was printed with the two rules aligned; every column that agrees is ticked in green as it is passed, and the first column that parts them, if there is one, is lit amber and stays lit.

wrong.why: reading a column backwards worked the first time, so doing it again looks like a check.
wrong.move: checks by reading the columns backwards a second time, the same way the digits were found.
wrong.screen: the same digit comes out a second time and is set beside the first, then the sum is added forwards and the column where the total parts from the printed answer is lit; the two backward readings and the one forward reading are all left standing on the stage together.

phases.screen: every card lifted and the forward check waiting
phases.soWhat: A digit you found is only right once the whole sum has been added forwards to the printed answer.
phases.concept: Adding it forwards is the check

writeup.delight: The third phase, the moment the answer digit is read against the digits above it. The two digits above the rule light deep blue and the answer digit under it stays green, and the too small light draws an amber ring around that answer digit and holds it. Then a single vermilion token lifts out of the column and settles in the circle above the column to its left, and the column reads its true total for a beat before closing back to the one digit that was printed. The digit that looked wrong is the digit that proves the carry. Nothing else moves and the voice says nothing while it happens.
writeup.opening: Every mount comes up already furnished for its phase with nothing in front of it. On the first phase a single finished ones column stands on the mat with one digit showing, one cover card lying over the digit beside it, and the answer digit in place under the rule. On the second a whole sum stands with cards in three of its columns, every column able to be tapped and none of them settled. On the third a tens column is showing whose answer digit is smaller than both of the digits above it. On the fourth every card has been lifted, the completed sum stands whole, and the forward check waits beside it. The running count at the top left holds the cards lifted against the cards lying on the sum, and the answer slot and the pad stand empty down the right. One thing moves, once: the cover card in the ones column, or the answer digit that looks too small, or the forward check control, gives one slow pulse while the voice says that the ones column is the way in. That pulse is the only invitation, and a finger on it is the whole way in.
writeup.freePlay: Any sum, any digits covered, with the reasoning strip, the too small light and the forward check open, and a build your own bay. Nothing to get right, no target and no timer. The child is left with the same stage and every control unlocked.
writeup.practice: Eight items over the four phases, easy first, on reading a column backwards, starting at the ones and allowing for a carry.
voiceLines: A finished sum with some digits hidden. The ones column is the way in.
The answer is showing. Work backwards to the digit that is hidden.
Start at the ones. Nothing can carry into it.
The answer digit looks too small. Where did the rest of it go?
Now add the whole thing forwards. Does it come to the answer that was printed?
Another sum, more cards. The same way in.
Free play. Cover any digits you like, in any sum, and hand it over.
Read the column again, and say what is known before you say what is missing.
You found every hidden digit, and then you added the whole thing forwards.

observations.why: No column can carry into the ones, so nothing can arrive in it from the right.
observations.soWhat: The ones column is always the way into a sum with digits hidden in it.
observations.observe: The ones column could be read with nothing else on the mat settled.

observations.why: Until the column on its right is settled, nobody knows whether a carry is coming in.
observations.soWhat: The order is not politeness; that column genuinely cannot be read yet.
observations.observe: A middle column tapped first was told which column came before it and nothing else.

observations.why: A column that passes nine keeps only its right hand digit.
observations.soWhat: The size of the answer digit says that the column traded, before any hidden digit is worked out.
observations.observe: An answer digit smaller than a digit above it meant a carry had left the column.

observations.why: Settling a column fixes what it carried out of itself.
observations.soWhat: The hunt moves left one column at a time, exactly the way a forward sum does.
observations.observe: Every digit that was found made the column to its left readable.

observations.why: A carry allowed for in the wrong place can still make one column come out.
observations.soWhat: The forward check is the only thing that reads the whole sum at once.
observations.observe: A digit that looked right in its own column was caught by adding forwards.

description: A finished sum with digits hidden under cards, and the only way in is the column on the far right.

mods.freeplay: Free Play. Any sum, any digits covered, with the reasoning strip and the forward check open.

source_tool.name: Missing Digit Detective
source_tool.blurb: A finished sum with digits hidden under cards, and the only way in is the column on the far right.

serves.exercise: writing the missing addends in the four given sums
finding the missing digits in the two printed sums

source_tool.description: A completed column sum stands on the mat with some of its digits covered by small cards. The answer row is never covered, so every column has enough in it to be reasoned about once the columns to its right have been settled. Tapping a column opens a reasoning strip that shows what is known in that column, what is missing and whether anything is coming in from the right, and the child types the digit into the covered square. A column tapped out of turn says which column has to be settled first rather than giving anything away, so the ones column is always the way in. When a column is settled and its total has passed nine, the carry appears in the circle above the next column by itself, which is what makes the next column solvable. A too small light marks any answer digit that is smaller than one of the digits above it, because that is the visible fingerprint of a carry leaving the column. When the last card is lifted the tool adds the whole sum forwards, column by column, against the answer that was printed, and either the two agree or the first column where they part is lit.
source_tool.art_direction: Cover cards on a finished column sum / Picture book

audio.note: Web Audio oscillators, no files. The same three cues in every tool of every Class 4 chapter, so the grade sounds like one grade.

wrong.note: A soft low double-bloop. A nudge, never a buzzer.

modes.note: THERE IS NO MODE AXIS ON THIS TOOL FAMILY. learn, practice and freeplay are gone and are not replaced by three of anything else: the axis itself is wrong for a tool a child works alone. See phase_mount.

authored.freeplay: Free Play. Any sum, any digits covered, with the reasoning strip and the forward check open.

modes.freePlay: Out of scope here. It is not reached from inside a phase mount, because a phase mount ends idle and has no finish card to reach it from. writeup.freePlay stays as the record of what that activity is, for whoever builds it as its own thing.

style.text: Least text. One header line, short labels, nothing else. The voice carries the teaching and the caption carries the voice.

stage.note: Every coordinate is authored in 1600x900, so a smartboard and a phone in landscape get one composition. Nothing scrolls. The three bands below are the settled layout, taken from Two Hundred Trail in Class 3 chapter 3 once it was finished; a tool that has to depart from one of them says in its own writeup.stage which band it changed and why.

bands.canvas: 92 to 746. One rounded panel holding everything the child works on.
bands.footer: 758 to 900. The voice at the far left, the phase bar at the right.
bands.header: 0 to 80. One line, and only one.

zones.bar: the phase bar at the right of the footer, the question count under it
zones.pad: under the slot, and furniture on every phase: twelve keys three across where a number is asked for, a word pad where a name or a rule is
zones.name: the tool name at the far left of the header, a measured dot set clear of it
zones.runs: the running count, on the canvas at its top left, never up in the chrome. It counts the thing the tool is actually building; where a tool has nothing to count that corner carries the record being kept instead, and that tool's own stage says so
zones.slot: the question and the child's answer, fixed down the right of the canvas
zones.work: the working area, one thousand and eighty-six by five hundred and twenty-eight
zones.title: the phase title beside that dot, on the same single header line
zones.voice: the caption at the far left of the footer, its speaking dot beside it
zones.chrome: again, sound and restart, as round controls at the far right of the header

stage.furniture: The working area is furnished from the first frame. What waits for the child is the count, not the picture: the panels, the slot and the pad are all up and empty before anything is asked.
stage.noSidebar: There is no sidebar. The canvas takes every unit the chrome can spare, because the working area is the tool.
stage.noScoreBox: There is no score box anywhere on the stage. The score leaves on the finished event and it is the host that decides whether to show it, so a child working is never watching a number that judges them.

style.motion: Animate only what carries meaning. Anything that is not changing does not move. Every reward is the maths itself moving, never confetti. Honour prefers-reduced-motion.
drawing: Hand-built inline SVG. No assets and no network, so a school cart works offline.
Chunky rounded forms and large touch targets. A finger is the pointer, not a mouse.

Drawn things, not abstract boxes: ruled column mats with a heading over every column, digit cards that can be picked up and dropped, bundles of ten that tie themselves together, a rule under the last addend, and a number line strip for the rounding work.

A sum is always shown with its columns visible: one digit to a column, every column under its named heading, the addends stacked with their right ends aligned, and a horizontal rule between the last addend and the sum. A bare row of digits with no column mat behind it is never used to teach adding.
A carried digit is always drawn small, above the column it is being added into, never in the margin and never below the rule.
Where tokens or bundles stand for a quantity, exactly the stated number of them is drawn and they stay countable at a glance and never overlap.
A column is told apart by its heading first and by its band second, so the stage still reads with the colour taken away.
style.palette_rule: A chrome colour never fills a digit, a column or a token the child is reading, and a content colour is never used for chrome. A number being added is deep blue, the sum under the rule is green, and a digit carried into the next column is vermilion, and those three are the same three colours in every tool and every picture of this chapter. A rounded number and any estimated sum are rose, so an estimate is told apart from an exact answer before either is read. The digit under discussion, which is usually the one that is missing, is amber. A zero holding a place open is grey, because it is a placeholder and not a quantity. All of that holds in greyscale, because a carry is told apart by being small and sitting above its column before it is told apart by its colour.

rules: Every spoken line is also printed in the caption line at the far left of the footer, so a muted tablet and a child who cannot hear lose nothing.
The caption stays in the footer. Nothing is ever written over the working area.

Numbers are written as words in every line and never as digits, so the voice says four steps and not 4 steps. Handed a digit, a synthesiser reads it in whatever register it likes and the chapter loses the words it is teaching.
The voice never gives the answer. It asks the same question a different way.
It speaks on opening, once when a phase begins, on a miss, and at the finish. It is silent otherwise; a tool that chatters gets muted, and then the first rule is all that is left.
props.muted is honoured at the source, and turning sound off cancels any line already speaking.
voice.where: The caption line sits at the far left of the footer with a small dot beside it that glows while the voice is talking. An again control repeats the last line.
voice.figure: None. The voice speaks with nothing on the stage.
voice.onMiss: Read the column again, and say what is known before you say what is missing.
voice.onNext: Another sum, more cards. The same way in.
voice.opening: A finished sum with some digits hidden. The ones column is the way in.
voice.onFinish: You found every hidden digit, and then you added the whole thing forwards.
voice.onFreePlay: Free play. Cover any digits you like, in any sum, and hand it over.
voice.figure_rule: A figure appears only where the printed chapter puts one and it has work to do. Everywhere else the voice speaks from the caption line with nothing on the stage: a mascot with no job is one more thing competing with the quantities the child is looking at.
voice.voicePreference: an English voice, female where one is offered

phase_map.concept: A column can be read backwards
Start at the ones here too
A carry explains an answer that looks too small
Adding it forwards is the check

placement.where: After a regrouping sum has been worked forwards and the carries can be pointed at. The tool is what keeps the columns honest, because it will not let a column be read before the one on its right is settled.

answer_key.rule: Work from the ones column leftwards, because nothing can carry into the ones and every other column may have a carry coming in. In each column, the digit that is missing is the one that makes the column come out to the answer digit, allowing for anything carried in and anything carried out. An answer digit smaller than a digit above it means the column passed nine and a carry left it. When every card is lifted, add the whole sum forwards and it must come to the answer that was printed.
answer_key.wrong: The reasoning strip for that column reopens with what is known lit and the incoming carry, if there is one, drawn into the circle. Nothing is cleared and nothing is marked.

hostProps.muted: Sound off. Honour it at the source, not by muting an element later. The captions carry on.
hostProps.phase: number, 1-based, which phase to build. The host chooses the activity; the component builds that phase and nothing else and never moves on by itself.
hostProps.device: tablet / web / smartboard. The stage is a fixed 1600x900 that scales; lay nothing out per device.
hostProps.audience: classroom or solo, and ACCEPTED AND NOT ACTED ON. The teach run and the hint ladder run either way. Kept so the contract is one shape across the book, and named here so nobody reads the shape as a promise.
hostProps.learnQuestions: The four worked items, one per phase, supplied by the host.
hostProps.practiceQuestions: The eight practice items, supplied by the host.

phase_mount.run: A phase is a complete activity in itself and it runs once. The teaching and the doing are not two screens and not two modes: the stage is furnished once, the voice talks over it, and the child starts working on the same stage without anything being rebuilt. Whatever the tool as a whole has to say goes into the FIRST phase's teach run, because there is no opening screen to say it on.
phase_mount.idle: NO AUTO-ADVANCE. After firing, the tool goes idle on the settled phase with the child's work still on it, and stops. Where the host supplies onNext it is drawn and it calls the host back; nothing in the component advances a phase.
phase_mount.prop: phase: number, 1-based, matching writeup.phases[].n. Rounded, clamped, and defaulting to 1 when the host sends nothing, so a bare mount is still a working tool rather than a blank screen. Read once: changing which phase a mount shows is a re-mount.
phase_mount.rule: ONE PHASE, ONE MOUNT. The host says which phase to build by passing `phase`, and the component builds that phase and nothing else. It does not know what came before it and it never moves on by itself.
phase_mount.opening: There is no opening panel and no Start button. The host has already chosen the activity, and a cover screen in front of it is a click between a child and the work. writeup.opening is the first frame of every mount rather than a panel of its own.
phase_mount.completion: The terminal event `finished`, with the phase in its detail, fired exactly once and guarded by a one-shot ref that only a restart re-arms, with the chime and the settle OUTSIDE the guard. props.onComplete is called alongside it: the event is the platform's signal and the callback is the host wrapper's, and firing only one of them leaves a child on a tool that never completes.
phase_mount.notInAMount: No finish card and no free play. Both are the host's now, built out of what the events told it. writeup.finish and writeup.freePlay stay as the record of what they are.

shared_state.note: What getState() returns. These names are a contract: the host reads them to persist and resume a child mid-activity, so renaming one breaks resume. `mode` is gone from this list because there is no mode. `phase` is the phase the host mounted, so a resume restores the work inside a phase and the host restores which phase.

agent_control.reason: Every tool in this chapter is child-operated. There is no agent-driven Concept mode, no postMessage command channel and no narration the tool waits on; the adult, where there is one, talks over the tool rather than through it.

steps: The column has to come to 9, because nothing was carried out of it.
One of the two digits is 6, so the other has to make up the rest.
items.question: In a ones column, 6 plus a hidden digit gives an answer digit of 9 and nothing is carried. What is the hidden digit?
items.checkpoint: With the answer showing and one digit known, the missing digit is fixed.
items.misconception: Writing 9, by reading the answer digit as the hidden digit.

steps: No digit added to 8 gives 5 on its own, so the column must have passed nine.
The column came to 15, because 15 is the only total past nine that ends in 5.
8 + 7 = 15, so the hidden digit is 7 and 1 ten is carried.
items.answer: 7, and 1 ten has been carried into the tens column
items.question: The ones column reads 8 plus a hidden digit and the answer digit is 5. What is the hidden digit, and what else has happened?
items.checkpoint: The ones column can always be read first, and it may send a carry left.
items.misconception: Deciding the column is impossible, because no digit added to 8 gives 5 without a carry.

steps: A column keeps only its right hand digit, so 6 is written.
The 1 that is left is a hundred, and it goes into the circle above the hundreds column.
items.answer: The column came to 16, so 6 was written and 1 hundred was carried
items.question: In a tens column, 6 and 9 are added with 1 carried in, and the answer digit is 6. Where did the rest go?
items.checkpoint: An answer digit smaller than the digits above it is the sign of a carry leaving.
items.misconception: Deciding the answer digit must be wrong because it is smaller than 9.

steps: Ones first: 7 + 8 = 15, so 5 is written and 1 is carried.
Tens: the hidden digit plus 6 plus the carried 1 has to end in 2, so the column came to 12 and the hidden digit is 5, carrying 1.
Hundreds: 5 plus the hidden digit plus the carried 1 has to end in 3, so the column came to 13 and the hidden digit is 7. Adding 4557 + 2768 forwards gives 7325.
items.answer: The tens digit of the first number is 5 and the hundreds digit of the second is 7, so 4557 + 2768 = 7325
items.question: Find both hidden digits and then check: 45_7 + 2_68 = 7325.
items.checkpoint: Every column is read with its incoming carry, and the finished sum is added forwards.
items.misconception: Finding a digit without allowing for the carry coming in, and never adding the sum forwards to catch it.

learn.selection: Fixed order, walking the phases from the first to the last.
learn.content_criterion: One per phase, so Learn walks the whole topic and stops.

items.question: In a ones column, 4 plus a hidden digit gives an answer digit of 9 and nothing is carried. What is the hidden digit?
In a hundreds column, a hidden digit plus 2 gives an answer digit of 8 and nothing is carried. What is the hidden digit?
Which column of a hidden digit sum can always be worked out first, and why?
items.final_answer: The ones column, because nothing can carry into it, so it is the only column that can be read on its own

items.question: The ones column reads 9 plus a hidden digit and the answer digit is 4. Find the hidden digit and say what is carried.
A tens column holds 8 and 7 with 1 carried in, and the answer digit is 6. Is that possible?
items.final_answer: Yes. The column comes to 16, so 6 is written and 1 hundred is carried

items.question: A child says a column adding 6 and 8 cannot have an answer digit of 4. What has the child forgotten?
items.final_answer: That the column comes to 14, so 4 is written and 1 is carried out of the column into the next one

items.question: Find the hidden digit and check by adding forwards: 36_5 + 2471 = 6146.
Find both hidden digits and check by adding forwards: 5_38 + 17_4 = 7412.
items.final_answer: The hundreds digit of the first number is 6 and the tens digit of the second is 7, so 5638 + 1774 = 7412

teaching_notes: This is the reasoning of the chapter and it deserves the slowest pace. Before anything is tapped, ask what is known in a column rather than what is missing, because a child who lists the known digits has already nearly finished. Keep the ones first lock on: being told which column comes first, without being told the answer, is what teaches the order, and the order is the lesson. When the too small light comes on, stop and get it said in words: the answer digit is smaller than the digits above it, so the column passed nine and a carry left. That sentence is the whole topic. Always finish with the forward check, even when everybody is sure. A digit found without allowing for its carry can look right in its own column and be caught nowhere else. The build your own bay is worth the last five minutes: a child who covers digits for a partner has to know which ones can still be found.
generation_prompt: Build a missing digit tool on a fixed 1600x900 SVG stage. A completed column sum sits on a ruled mat with named headings and a circle above each column, with small cover cards over some addend digits; the answer row is never covered. Tapping a column opens a reasoning strip beneath the mat showing the known digits, the gap and any carry coming in, with a numeric pad for the answer. A column tapped before the column to its right is settled is refused and the column that must come first is lit, giving nothing else away. Settling a column whose total passes nine drops the carry into the circle above the next column automatically. A too small light outlines any answer digit smaller than a digit above it. When every card is lifted, an add it forwards control works the completed sum column by column against the printed answer and lights the first column where they differ. A build your own bay lets a child enter a correct sum and cover digits in it. Pointer events only, no assets, no network. Build it from the writeup and the tool build spec, not from this paragraph (maths_agent/TOOL_BUILD_SPEC.md). The three bands and every measurement come from writeup.stage and tool_config.style.stage: one header line, one canvas panel holding everything the child works on with the running count at its top left and the question, slot and pad fixed down its right as furniture, and a footer with the voice at the far left and the phase bar at the right. No sidebar, and no score box anywhere. One phase, one mount: build the phase the host passes and nothing else (tool_config.phase_mount). The first frame comes from writeup.opening. Each phase comes from writeup.phases, with its screen, action, reward and spoken line; its tries field is the hint ladder and its wrong list is what the stage does about a wrong answer, redrawn in steps on the working area with nothing marked and nothing reset. The one surprise is writeup.delight. The look and the sounds come from tool_config.style, voice and audio.
instructions_for_student: Tap the ones column first, because nothing can carry into it. Work out the hidden digit from what is showing, then move one column to the left and take any carry with you. When every card is lifted, add the whole sum forwards and see whether it comes to the answer that was printed.
